# Energy

Efficient and rational use of energy

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [Environmental Sustainability](https://www.eafit.edu.co/sostenibilidad-ambiental)
- Energy

##### Efficient and rational use of energy

Electricity is present in most of our daily activities, making it crucial to find ways to conserve it. This component aims to implement strategies focused on reducing consumption and promoting the rational use of electricity consumed for all activities and services at EAFIT University.

Some of these strategies include taking advantage of natural light in spaces and new designs, implementing efficient technologies and sustainable practices.

###### Actions:

Implementation of the KNX system: This allows for the control of lighting in different buildings and spaces across the campus. 32% of the office lighting can be remotely controlled by turning it on, off, or dimming it. It is also possible to program the on/off switching of lighting on the main campus, the southern campus, and in Pereira.

Implementation of the PME system: allows monitoring of general energy consumption in some blocks and particular areas in the main, South, Pereira and Llanogrande headquarters (lighting, outlets (power) and air conditioning).

15% of the campus lighting is LED type.

Solar panels have been installed on the roofs of blocks 19 and 1, supplying 6% of the photovoltaic energy for the campus.

29% of the air conditioning equipment installed uses direct expansion, while 71% uses chilled water. The latter refers to a centralized air conditioning system that optimizes its operation.

The chilled water plant allows for savings of between 30% and 50% of the electrical energy needed to cool the water required in the air conditioning system.

The security cameras were upgraded, resulting in a decrease in electricity consumption from 30W to 15W.

73% of classrooms have dimmable lighting

73% of classrooms have presence sensors for turning lights on and off.

32% of office lighting can be controlled remotely (KNX)

83% of bathrooms have presence sensors for turning lights on and off.

70% of the blocks have energy consumption measurement (lighting, power and electromechanical equipment)

71% of the blocks have equipment connected to the chilled water plant that supplies the AC system
